# Product Hunt

5 endpoints, all GET. Base URL `https://www.socialcrawl.dev`, auth header `x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY`.

**Credit costs:** 5 standard (1 credit) - the exact cost is in each endpoint heading below.

## GET /v1/producthunt/launches - 1 credit (standard)

Returns the launches Product Hunt is currently featuring, roughly 50 of them, each with its post ID, product name (post.ext.title), tagline (post.content.text), product page URL, the maker's display name, post.published_at (when the post was created, which can be weeks before its launch day) and post.ext.updated_at. Order is the feed's own and is not the vote ranking. Votes, comments and makers' handles are not available on this endpoint, so those fields are null. Narrow the list with topic, a Product Hunt topic slug such as artificial-intelligence, and filter it with query.

**Use when** you want to spot new products in a category before they spread, or to check whether a problem already has a fresh launch.
**Cost** cache 120 s
**Empty results** An upstream 404 means "zero items", not "not found" - you get `200 {items: []}` and a refund.
**Paging** single page - The upstream feed is one document of about 50 entries with no pagination: page, day and before were probed 22/09/2026 and are ignored. Every entry the feed holds is returned in one call.

**Query params**

- `topic` (optional, string) - Product Hunt topic slug, as in producthunt.com/topics/<slug>, for example artificial-intelligence or developer-tools. A display name such as Developer Tools is converted to its slug. An unrecognised topic returns no launches, with a note in data._warnings, and costs nothing. · e.g. `artificial-intelligence`
- `query` (optional, string) - Case-insensitive text filter applied to the product name and tagline of the current launches. It filters this feed; it does not search Product Hunt's archive.
- `since` (optional, string) - Rows published from this date: YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC) or ISO 8601. Rows older than it are left off each page. This list is not in date order, so the walk does not stop at the date: keep following `next_cursor`, and each page costs what a page costs even when every row on it is filtered out. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until).
- **Shared controls** `until` → [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until)

**Response** `PostList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ computed, post }` ([full schema](schemas/PostList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `post.content.text` | Post caption, description, or text content |
| `post.ext.title` | The post title on its own. |
| `post.id` | Platform-specific post ID… |
| `post.published_at` | Post creation timestamp as an ISO 8601 UTC string. |
| `post.url` | Direct URL to the post on the source platform |
| `computed.content_category` | Keyword-classified content category… |

+7 more (types in the full schema): `computed` {engagement_rate, estimated_reach, language, save_rate}; `post.author` {display_name}; `post.ext` {updated_at}; `post.flags` {deleted}. Also in the sample: `post.flags` {nsfw null, spoiler null, pinned null}. Never filled: `post.author.avatar_url`, `post.author.username`, `post.author.verified`, `post.content.duration_seconds`, `post.content.media_urls`, `post.content.thumbnail_url`, `post.engagement.comments`, `post.engagement.likes`, `post.engagement.saves`, `post.engagement.shares`, `post.engagement.views`. Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/producthunt/launches" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/producthunt/leaderboard - 1 credit (standard)

Returns Product Hunt's ranked launches for one day, week, month or year, back to 2013: rank, product name (post.ext.title), tagline, link, thumbnail, upvotes (post.engagement.likes), comment count, launch time and topics. Promoted placements are left out, and data._warnings says so when the board had any. Pass the returned cursor for more of a long board.

**Use when** you want to see what won a period, back to 2013. Promoted placements are left out.
**Cost** cache 1800 s
**Empty results** An upstream 404 means "zero items", not "not found" - you get `200 {items: []}` and a refund.
**Paging** cursor · ≈17/page (observed once); set with `limit` · depth unknown · N items ≈ ceil(N/17) x 1 credits

**Query params**

- `period` (optional, enum: daily | weekly | monthly | yearly) - daily (default), weekly, monthly or yearly. · e.g. `daily`
- `date` (optional, string) - The day to read, YYYY-MM-DD, for a daily board. Default today. · e.g. `2014-06-10`
- `year` (optional, integer, 2013-2100) - The year, for a weekly, monthly or yearly board.
- `month` (optional, integer, 1-12) - The month, 1 to 12, for a monthly board.
- `week` (optional, integer, 1-53) - The ISO week, 1 to 53, for a weekly board.
- `limit` (optional, integer, 1-20) - Rows to return, 1 to 20. Default 20.
- `cursor` (optional, string) - Continuation token from a previous response's pagination block, passed back with the same parameters. Omit for the first page.
- `since` (optional, string) - Rows published from this date: YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC) or ISO 8601. Rows older than it are left off each page. This list is not in date order, so the walk does not stop at the date: keep following `next_cursor`, and each page costs what a page costs even when every row on it is filtered out. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until).
- **Shared controls** `max_pages` (1-50) → [walks](api-overview.md#search-filters-and-multi-page-walks); `max_items` (1-5000) · `max_credits` (1-100000) → [one-call walks](api-overview.md#get-more-in-one-call-max_items-max_credits-max_pages); `until` → [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until)

**Response** `PostList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ computed, post }` ([full schema](schemas/PostList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `post.content.text` | Post caption, description, or text content |
| `post.ext.title` | The post title on its own. |
| `post.id` | Platform-specific post ID… |
| `post.published_at` | Post creation timestamp as an ISO 8601 UTC string. |
| `post.url` | Direct URL to the post on the source platform |
| `computed.content_category` | Keyword-classified content category… |

+9 more (types in the full schema): `computed` {engagement_rate, estimated_reach, language, save_rate}; `post.content` {thumbnail_url}; `post.engagement` {comments, likes}; `post.ext` {hashtags}; `post.flags` {deleted}. Also in the sample: `post.flags` {nsfw null, spoiler null, pinned null}; `post.ext` {mentions null}. Never filled: `post.author.avatar_url`, `post.author.display_name`, `post.author.username`, `post.author.verified`, `post.content.duration_seconds`, `post.content.media_urls`, `post.engagement.saves`, `post.engagement.shares`, `post.engagement.views`. Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`, `data.walk`.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/producthunt/leaderboard" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/producthunt/product - 1 credit (standard)

Returns one Product Hunt product: tagline, description, website and domain, followers, review count and rating, number of launches, categories, social links and screenshots, plus its latest launch with upvotes, launch-day upvotes, comments, launch number and daily, weekly and monthly rank. include_launches adds every launch the product has had.

**Use when** you want to profile a product and see how its latest launch performed. Set include_launches to get every launch.
**Cost** cache 900 s
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `id` (optional, string) - The product slug, for example notion. Send id or url. · e.g. `notion`
- `url` (optional, string) - A Product Hunt product link, for example https://www.producthunt.com/products/notion.
- `include_launches` (optional, boolean) - true to add every launch the product has had. Default false.

**Constraints**

- Provide at least one of `id`, `url`.

**Response** `Analytics` object at `data` (inferred from a sample): {id string, slug string, name string, tagline string, description string, url string, website_url string, website_domain string, logo_url string, followers_count number, reviews_count number, reviews_rating number, launches_count number, is_no_longer_online boolean, is_top_product boolean, categories string[], screenshots string[]}; `social_links` {twitter string, instagram string, linkedin string, angellist string, ios string, android string}; `launch` {id string, name string} (+13 more).

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/producthunt/product" \
  --data-urlencode "id=notion" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/producthunt/product/comments - 1 credit (standard)

Returns the discussion under a product's launch, threads flattened in order with each reply's comment.parent_id: text, votes (comment.engagement.likes), reply count, pinned flag, time, and the commenter's username, name and avatar. Pass the returned cursor for the next page.

**Use when** you want to read what the community said on launch day, including how the maker answered.
**Cost** cache 300 s
**Empty results** An upstream 404 means "zero items", not "not found" - you get `200 {items: []}` and a refund.
**Paging** cursor · default page size not measured; set with `limit` · depth unknown

**Query params**

- `url` (required) - A Product Hunt product link or slug, for example notion. · e.g. `notion`
- `limit` (optional, integer, 1-20) - Rows to return, 1 to 20. Default 20.
- `cursor` (optional, string) - Continuation token from a previous response's pagination block, passed back with the same parameters. Omit for the first page.
- `since` (optional, string) - Rows published from this date: YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC) or ISO 8601. Rows older than it are left off each page. This list is not in date order, so the walk does not stop at the date: keep following `next_cursor`, and each page costs what a page costs even when every row on it is filtered out. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until).
- **Shared controls** `max_pages` (1-50) → [walks](api-overview.md#search-filters-and-multi-page-walks); `max_items` (1-5000) · `max_credits` (1-100000) → [one-call walks](api-overview.md#get-more-in-one-call-max_items-max_credits-max_pages); `until` → [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until)

**Response** `CommentList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ comment, computed }` ([full schema](schemas/CommentList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `comment.text` | Comment body. |
| `comment.id` | Platform-specific comment ID (always a string) |
| `comment.published_at` | Comment creation timestamp as an ISO 8601 UTC string. |
| `comment.url` | Direct URL to the comment on the source platform |
| `comment.author.username` | Comment author username (null when tombstoned) |
| `comment.parent_id` | Parent comment ID for nested replies, or null for… |

+9 more (types in the full schema): `comment` {post_id}; `comment.author` {avatar_url, display_name}; `comment.engagement` {likes, replies}; `comment.ext` {author_url}; `comment.flags` {deleted, pinned}; `computed` {language}. Never filled: `comment.author.verified`. Page-level: `data.comment_recency`, `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`, `data.walk`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/producthunt/product/comments" \
  --data-urlencode "url=notion" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/producthunt/topic - 1 credit (standard)

Returns the products in one Product Hunt topic: name, tagline, link, logo, followers, review count and rating, number of launches and the latest launch, plus the topic itself in data.topic. Pass the returned cursor for the next page.

**Use when** you want to survey a product category and see which products lead it.
**Cost** cache 1800 s
**Empty results** An upstream 404 means "zero items", not "not found" - you get `200 {items: []}` and a refund.
**Paging** cursor · ≈20/page (observed once); set with `limit` · depth unknown · N items ≈ ceil(N/20) x 1 credits

**Query params**

- `topic` (optional, string) - A topic slug, for example artificial-intelligence. · e.g. `artificial-intelligence`
- `limit` (optional, integer, 1-20) - Rows to return, 1 to 20. Default 20.
- `cursor` (optional, string) - Continuation token from a previous response's pagination block, passed back with the same parameters. Omit for the first page.
- **Shared controls** `max_pages` (1-50) → [walks](api-overview.md#search-filters-and-multi-page-walks); `max_items` (1-5000) · `max_credits` (1-100000) → [one-call walks](api-overview.md#get-more-in-one-call-max_items-max_credits-max_pages)

**Constraints**

- `topic` is required (it is optional in shape only - the request needs it).

**Response** `SearchResult` rows at `data.items[]` (inferred from a sample): {id string, slug string, name string, tagline string, url string, logo_url string, reviews_count number, reviews_rating number, followers_count number, launches_count number, is_no_longer_online boolean}; `latest_launch` {id string, slug null, name null, scheduled_at string}.

Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`, `data.topic`, `data.walk`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/producthunt/topic" \
  --data-urlencode "topic=artificial-intelligence" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```
